title: alert-story-templates-and-investigation-checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical working set of short, repeatable alert story templates and an investigation checklist tailored for tokenized LLM inference (hosted + dedicated + private). Aim: speed up first-10-minutes triage, keep comms tight, and capture enough context for postmortems.

Scope and intended users:
- Oncall engineers (ops / SRE / serving runtime)
- Solutions engineers / SEs who own customer comms when tenants are impacted
- Product/eng stakeholders doing post-incident analysis

How to use:
- When an alert fires, pick the closest "story template" below, fill it out and paste into PagerDuty/Slack channel. Use the checklist for quick probes.
- If the root cause isn't obvious after the checklist, escalate per the matrix at the bottom.

ALERT STORY TEMPLATE (short form — single paragraph for initial comms)
- Title: [brief one-line, e.g. "High p95 latency for hosted/text-generation east-us-1"]
- Time window: [first observed / now]
- Scope: [models, routes, customers, percentage of requests affected]
- Observable signal(s): [e.g. p95 token_latency, queue_depth, gpu_util, kv_cache_miss_rate]
- Impact: [user-facing latency, failed requests, cost spike, customer-reported outages]
- Immediate action taken: [fallback routing, scale up, throttling, rollback]
- Next step / owner: [who is leading triage + ETA for update]

Example initial story (copy/paste):
"Title: High p95 request latency for hosted/generation in us-east-1. First seen 2026-01-12T09:41Z, ongoing. Impact: ~8% of requests show p95 > 1.2s and increased queue_depth on pool:hosted-gen-eus, several customers report slow chat responses. Signals: p95 token_latency spiked from 350ms -> 1.1s, gpu_util on node-group-3 at 98%, kv_cache_miss_rate up 6x. Immediate mitigation: autoscaler bumped 2 instances and a canary fallback route enabled. Owner: @aisha (ETA update in 10m)."

ALERT STORY TEMPLATE (detailed for Slack/PD followups)
- Title
- Incident ID (PD id)
- Start / detected times
- Topline impact summary (one sentence)
- Affected tenants / customer list (if known)
- Quantitative impact: p50/p95/p99, error rate deltas, token cost delta, queue depth change
- Prominent traces / span ids (links)
- Quick hypothesis (3 bullets)
- Immediate mitigations tried and result
- Next actions and owners (who will take which probe)
- Communications plan (external status page / customer comms)

QUICK INVESTIGATION CHECKLIST (first 10 minutes)
1) Validate signal
   - Confirm metric window and aggregation (ex: p95 over 5m vs 1m). Check dashboard timeshift to 30m/2h.
2) Scope & blast radius
   - Is this global, region-specific, model-specific, or tenant-specific?
   - Run: filter by model, route, tenant-id. Check top-10 tenants by request volume.
3) Fast probes (infra-level)
   - GPU/memory: current utilization % and recent jumps per node-group. Look at GPU temperature/warnings.
   - Node status: pod restarts, OOMs, GPU driver errors in last 5m.
   - Autoscaler activity: Did a scale event coincide? Any failed scale attempts?
4) Serving runtime probes
   - KV cache warmth metric: prefix_kv_warmth and eviction rate => cold-start wave?
   - Batch size distribution: did average batch size drop (indicating many singleton flows)?
   - Queue depth and backlog per model shard: queue_depth > backlog_threshold?
5) Tracing anchor check
   - Grab a 10-sample of traces from the spike window. Look for common slow spans (kv_lookup, model_infer, token_emit).
   - Confirm whether latency is at model kernel time or pre/post processing (tokenizer, network).
6) Downstream checks
   - Upstream client change?: sudden increase in prefix length or prompt size? Check token count distributions.
   - Downstream storage/db throttling? (rare but check if traces show DB calls).
7) Apply quick mitigations (if safe)
   - Route heavy customers to dedupe/queue or to a lower-cost model variant.
   - Increase pool capacity or enable dedicated short-term burst.
   - Toggle small config flags: reduce max_tokens, reduce max concurrency per tenant.
8) Communication + ticketing
   - Post initial story to PD channel + #inc-ops slack. Tag affected SEs/AMs for customers.

Dashboard lane checklist (what to keep visible in an investigation dashboard)
- Topline lane: p50/p95/p99 request latency, request rate, error rate (per route/model/tenant)
- Capacity lane: GPU util %, active GPU count, node restarts, autoscaler events
- Queueing lane: queue_depth per model-shard, average batch size, batching latency (ms)
- Cache lane: kv_cache_hit_rate, eviction_rate, prefix_hit_ratio, warm_start_count
- Cost lane (quick): token/sec, token_cost_rate (approx) — to detect runaway cost spikes
- Trace anchor lane: list of recent slow spans with timestamps + quick links to span view
- Tenant impact lane: top impacted tenants (by failed requests or increased latency)

Tracing anchor conventions (short notes)
- Span naming: service.infer -> model.kernel -> model.kv_lookup -> model.postproc -> response.serialize
- Important tags: tenant_id, route, model_version, seq_len, prefix_id, batch_size, node_id
- When sampling: for latency spikes sample 100% for requests exceeding p99 latency; otherwise probabilistic by tenant-weight.
- Attach a short sample payload snippet (redact PII) for every slow trace captured.

Quick SQL/metrics query examples (adapt to existing metrics store)
- p95 by model in window: SELECT model, percentile(latency_ms,95) FROM inference.requests WHERE ts > now()-10m GROUP BY model ORDER BY percentile DESC LIMIT 10
- KV miss spike probe: SELECT ts, sum(kv_misses) as misses FROM inference.kvcache WHERE region='us-east-1' and ts > now()-30m GROUP BY ts ORDER BY ts DESC
- Batch size collapse check: SELECT avg(batch_size) FROM inference.batches WHERE ts > now()-20m GROUP BY minute(ts)

Escalation decision matrix (summary)
- If >10% top-line traffic affected OR revenue-affecting customer on degraded service -> page SRE + serving-runtime lead immediately.
- If spike persists >30m after mitigations with no clear root cause -> engage infra on-call (GPU infra) and platform-eng to check autoscaler and node provisioning.
- If data privacy/sensitive customer tenants impacted -> follow security runbook and notify Security and Legal per compliance path.

Ownership mapping (who to call)
- Serving runtime performance / batching / KV cache: eng-serving-runtime (primary)
- Autoscaler / infra provisioning: platform-engineering
- Tenant-facing comms / account triage: solutions-engineering-and-professional-services
- Tracing and observability widgets: eng-observability

Post-incident: incident story skeleton for postmortem (what to capture)
- One-line summary + timeline (events with timestamps)
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence mapping (metrics/traces that support each hypothesis)
- Mitigations (short-term and longer term)
- Owner(s) for fixes and ETA
- What we learned (2–3 clear takeaways)
- Open follow-ups with ticket IDs

Small operator cheat-list (copyable into Slack thread)
- "Probe1: checking p95 by model -> <metrics link>"
- "Probe2: fetching last 10 traces over p99 -> <trace link>"
- "Mitigation: scaled pool hosted-gen-eus by +2 (id:autoscale-345)"
- "Next: Leah@eng-observability to assemble dashboard snapshot for postmortem"

Conservative templates for customer-facing status (short):
- "We are investigating increased latency for text generation in US-East. We have scaled capacity and enabled fallback routing. We will provide another update in 30 minutes. Customers experiencing persistent issues can reply to this thread."

Open questions / TODOs (notes for follow-up experiments)
- What threshold for kv_cache_miss_rate should auto-trigger a pre-warm job? (experiment needed)
- Add a single-click dashboard tile that shows top-10 slow spans with direct trace links (engineering effort estimate?)
- Validate whether batch_size drop correlates more strongly with client-side small-prompt patterns or server-side throttling; add metric to capture client prompt-size changes.
- Run a tabletop using this template with SRE + SEs next oncall rotation (simulate cold-start burst).

References / links (placeholders)
- Incident runbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood/example-obs-runbook
- PagerDuty play: PD escalation -> SRE primary -> platform-eng -> infra
- Trace viewer: https://traces.redwood.example/samples

Notes to self / rough ideas (informal)
- Might be useful to draft a tiny UI flow in Console that auto-populates the Alert Story Template when an alert is acknowledged (copy to clipboard).
- Consider short tick-box checklist on the incident page to ensure comms steps are executed (customer notification, status page, postmortem owner).

If you iterate on this doc, keep initial story short — one paragraph — and move detailed hypothesis into the incident thread.

-- Aisha (draft)
